items.heading: Forensic Science Is a Genuinely
items.text: Forensic science is a genuinely growing field in India right now, and it is not the niche, crowded specialism some online chatter suggests. A 2023 legal reform, the BNSS, made forensic investigation mandatory for serious crimes, and the resulting demand has been real: the Bureau of Police Research and Development recorded a 12% annual rise in forensic science jobs between 2022 and 2024.

items.heading: Compared with Most Other Science
items.text: Compared with most other science degrees, this question carries two extra layers most families never weigh together: a 2023 law just legally mandated the entire field's core work, and getting hired depends almost entirely on clearing a specific government exam, not on the college brand printed on the degree.

items.heading: Before Comparing Pay or Tracks,
items.text: Before comparing pay or tracks, it helps to see the actual daily texture of the work, not the version that shows up in a crime-drama episode or a college brochure.

rows: Lab/Scientific Assistant, state Forensic Science Laboratory (entry, govt)

The most common entry point, filled through a state recruitment exam (UPSSSC, state PSC, or a department-specific test), not a campus placement. Pay follows a government scale with DA and increments, so it looks modest on day one but is stable and rises on a fixed ladder.
Scientific Officer, state FSL or Central Forensic Science Laboratory (post-exam, degree-qualified)

Requires clearing a genuinely competitive written exam plus interview, usually needing an NFSU or other recognised M.Sc/B.Sc forensic science degree. This is the real step in this field, not a professional licence, and it is why hundreds of private-college graduates never actually reach a lab bench.

Reached through seniority, further qualification (M.Sc or PhD), and internal promotion exams over 5-10+ years. Pay ceilings here are real but slow, set by government pay-scale structure rather than individual negotiation.
Digital/cyber forensic analyst, private sector (banks, fintech, law firms, cybersecurity firms)
Rs 5-9 LPA entry, climbing to Rs 15-20+ LPA with 5+ years

India's digital forensics sector faces a shortage of roughly 90,000 trained professionals against a market projected to reach $1.39 billion by 2030. That shortage is exactly why digital and cyber forensic specialists typically earn 30-40% more than traditional forensic lab roles.

items.heading: Unlike Architecture or Medicine, There
items.text: Unlike architecture or medicine, there is no professional licensing body deciding who can practise forensic science. The step instead is a state or central government recruitment exam plus interview, run separately from any college's admission or placement process.
